newsitem.title: USA: More troops may go to Bosnia for vote -Joulwan.
newsitem.headline: More troops may go to Bosnia for vote -Joulwan.

text.p: The NATO-led peacekeeping force in Bosnia could be increased by up to 3,000 troops in September to protect civilians voting in municipal elections, the alliance's supreme allied commander said on Monday.

But U.S. Army Gen. George Joulwan, commander of NATO forces in Europe, stressed in comments to reporters that no decision had yet been made on any addition. There are now some 31,000 peacekeepers from 34 nations in Bosnia, including 8,500 U.S. troops.

"I hate to speculate until I know all the requirements, but we have looked at a range up to and including four to six battalions if it comes to that. But we are not at that stage yet," Joulwan said at a Pentagon news conference on the military mission in Bosnia.
"That may be upwards of, I would say, two or three thousands personnel. I am not sure how many Americans. It is a NATO commitment that we are talking about," he added.

Bosnia municipal elections, which have been postponed several times, are now tentatively scheduled for Sept. 13-14. Joulwan said NATO was committed to helping the Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) assure that elections will be held in a stable atmosphere.
He said that the number of additional troops required would probably depend on whether the tense areas of Mostar and Brcko were included in the voting.
